title: Chain with subtask which are not registered raises NotImplementedError: Tasks must define the run method.
body:
See the following example:

celery_app.py:

``` python
from celery import Celery, chain, subtask

celery = Celery('tasks', broker='redis://localhost/0', backend='redis://localhost/0')

#@celery.task(name="worker.add")
#def add(a, b):
#    pass
#
#@celery.task(name="worker.sub")
#def sub(result):
#    pass


g = chain(subtask("worker.add", (2, 2)) | subtask("worker.sub", (1, )))
print g().get()
```

celery_worker.py:

``` python
from celery import Celery

celery = Celery('tasks', broker='redis://localhost/0', backend='redis://localhost/0')

@celery.task(name="worker.add")
def add(x, y):
    return x + y

@celery.task(name="worker.sub")
def sub(result, x):
    return result - x
```

Start the worker with:

``` bash
# celery worker -A celery_worker 
```

When the task is called:

``` bash
# python celery_app.py                                                                                                                              
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "celery_app.py", line 16, in <module>
    print g().get()
  File "/Users/italorossi/envs/test/lib/python2.7/site-packages/celery/result.py", line 108, in get
    interval=interval)
  File "/Users/italorossi/envs/test/lib/python2.7/site-packages/celery/backends/base.py", line 185, in wait_for
    raise result
NotImplementedError: Tasks must define the run method.
```

Uncommenting these lines on celery_app.py:

``` python
#@celery.task(name="worker.add")
#def add(a, b):
#    pass
#
#@celery.task(name="worker.sub")
#def sub(result):
#    pass
```

Solves the problem. The run method on the task is correctly created and everything works as expected.

This is the same problem as described here:
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!msg/celery-users/AmYdBOo2H3w/w1WgIxdJjfAJ

I've tested with celery 3.0.24 and the problem persists.
